say: A busy reader decides in seconds. So the subject says what the email is about and what you need. Never leave it blank or write only hello.

panel.heading: Five parts of a good email
items: Subject: what it is about and what you need
Greeting: Dear Mrs Okafor, or Dear Admissions Team
Purpose in the first line
Details: dates, amounts, what is attached
Next step, closing, your name and phone

say: Greet the reader properly. If you do not know the name, write Dear Admissions Team.

Email can be kept forever, so never write your BVN, card details, PIN or password in one.

say: Phishing is a message that pretends to come from someone you trust, to steal your password, OTP, card details or money. By SMS it is called smishing.

panel.heading: A real message or a phishing message?
left: Never asks for your PIN or OTP
right: Display name hides a Gmail address
Asks for PIN, OTP, BVN or card

say: Watch for fear and urgency, prizes you did not expect, and requests for secrets. Real banks do not ask for these by email, SMS or call.
The bold name in Gmail is only a display name. Tap it to see the real address. Zenith Bank Security sending from a Gmail address is a scam.

panel.heading: A real message or a phishing message?

right: Display name hides a Gmail address

say: Esther in Abuja got an SMS asking for a 1,250 naira customs fee to release her parcel. First, she paused, and read the link. It was a strange domain.

panel.heading: What to do with a suspicious message

cards.d: Press and hold a link to read the domain. Do not open attachments or reply.
Use the shop's own email or app, or call the friend or the number on your card.
Change the password at once. If you shared bank details or an OTP, call your bank now.

say: Then she used the tracking link in the shop's own email. No fee was due. If a friend's WhatsApp asks for money, call them on a normal phone call first.

panel.heading: What to do with a suspicious message

cards.d: Press and hold a link to read the domain. Do not open attachments or reply.

Change the password at once. If you shared bank details or an OTP, call your bank now.

say: If you already typed something, act at once. Change the password and turn on two-step verification. If you shared bank details or an OTP, call the number on your card. Speed matters more than embarrassment.

say: To remember. Add your recovery details on day one. Use Bcc for groups. Put your message in the subject and first line.
Tap the display name to see who really sent it. And when a message rushes you, pause and check through a channel you already trust.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Add a recovery phone and recovery email on day one
Bcc hides addresses in group emails
Subject and first line carry your main message
Tap the display name to see the real sender
Pause, check another way, then report
